items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] We are in Clearwater Beach at the Arbors Jazz Fest and my name is Monk Rowe. I’m very pleased to have Sherrie Maricle with me today.

ctx.x: Sherrie Maricle was born in Buffalo, New York on September 2, 1963. She currently balances a career as a drummer, band leader, composer and educator. Sherrie has performed with Clark Terry, Dizzy Gillespie and Slam Stewart, and records with the Diva Big Band and her quintet, Five Play.
Sherrie was interviewed in Clearwater Beach, Florida on March 18, 2001, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

We are in Clearwater Beach at the Arbors Jazz Fest and my name is Monk Rowe. I’m very pleased to have Sherrie Maricle with me today. And usually I say saxophonist somebody or, you know, keyboardist, but I’m not sure which to go first with you. I was looking at your write-up and I don’t know how you handle your life.

items.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Sherrie Maricle addresses the interviewer as 'Monk' multiple times (e.g., 'I know, Monk, that’s such a great point', 'Hey, Monk, there’s a — I did a tour...').

ctx.x: Yeah. We’re hoping that those venues and festivals can still exist in 2021.

I know, Monk, that’s such a great point, and you know recently, well last week reading things about great iconic clubs in New York like Small’s that are really — major performance clubs, of course the Blue Note, the Vanguard, Dizzy’s, and Jazz Standard and those places, I’m assuming have enough, are financially secure to survive this. But other iconic clubs that are really like the heart and soul that give so many artists an opportunity like Small’s and Mezzro and Fat Cat and they’re like you said, I don’t know…

I had a question that I’ve tried to hone down but I haven’t really done it yet, but are there things that you do now, or let’s say up until March, over the years, that took a lot of time and energy and assuming that at some point we get back to normal, you would think twice about actually doing them again because you’ve noticed that your life is easier because you’re not?
